findings.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — An unauthenticated GET with any crafted embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that creates a brand-new public topic, so distinct query strings on the allowed host give an attacker unlimited unthrottled topic/post creation.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — url` is interpolated into `<a href='#{url}'>` with no escaping, so an attacker-supplied embed_url containing a quote (URI parses `https://host/p?x='/onmouseover='...` fine) injects attributes into a post that is later rendered raw.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Feed HTML is CGI.unescapeHTML'd (actively un-escaping `<script>`) and imported with cook_method raw_html and no sanitizer, so a feed item body becomes stored XSS for every viewer.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue: one bad item (e.g. a feed with no content:encoded makes `i.content` nil and `nil.scrub` raise) aborts the whole loop and, with `retry: false`, silently drops every remaining item.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The only access control on this public endpoint is `request.referer`, an attacker-supplied header, so the embeddable-host gate passes for any direct curl request while appearing to enforce framing.
lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The return value of `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` is discarded, so a failed save is indistinguishable from an applied revision.
lib/post_revisor.rb:21 — revise!` returns true unconditionally once `should_revise?` passes, reporting success to callers even when the underlying save failed.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1` is advanced with `update_column` regardless of whether `revise!` actually applied the revision, so a failed update is permanently masked from the line 34 change check and never retried.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — post.present?` is true even when PostCreator rolled back (it returns the unsaved Post object), so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with a nil `post_id` and raises a NOT NULL violation instead of skipping.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` can be nil once the post is deleted (no FK, no dependent cleanup), and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed run.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s and each reload re-enters `best` and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job, so any URL that can never be imported becomes a permanent self-amplifying job loop per open browser tab.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — A regular job synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed, bypassing PollFeed's `sidekiq_options retry: false` so a poison feed is re-downloaded and re-imported on every RetrieveTopic retry.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` is a TOCTOU check against the unique index: a concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic both pass it and the loser raises RecordNotUnique, killing the whole run.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever, and the key is claimed before any work so failed retrievals are throttled like successful ones.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The throttle key embeds the full attacker-controlled embed_url, so unbounded distinct URLs of unbounded length produce unbounded distinct redis keys.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — no_throttle` is granted for any request carrying a staff session, so a logged-in staff member browsing an embedded page bypasses the 60s throttle and triggers a full synchronous feed poll on every page load.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` follows redirects without re-validating the host and ignores port/userinfo, so an open redirect on the embeddable host turns the public endpoint into an SSRF whose response body is imported into a public post.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — revise!` is called without `bypass_bump`, so a source page whose HTML changes on every fetch bumps the topic to the top of the latest list every hour forever.
app/models/post.rb:133 — cook` returns raw verbatim for raw_html posts with no allowlist, and the flag is sticky, so every later edit of that post by any user is also stored unsanitized.
lib/post_creator.rb:216 — :cook_method` is now forwarded from arbitrary PostCreator opts, so any caller that passes user-controlled params through can request the sanitizer-bypassing raw_html mode.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — The `revise!` + `update_column` pair runs outside any transaction, so a crash between them leaves the post revised while the sha1 stays stale and the item is re-revised on the next poll.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — params.require(:embed_url)` accepts non-strings, so `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` turns the lookup into an IN-clause matching an unrelated topic and `embed_url[k]=v` produces an unhandled 500.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — Every test mocks `poll_feed`, so the feed fetch, parsing, per-item error handling and import path have zero coverage and stay green regardless of production behaviour.
spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — Both throttle tests stub `retrieved_recently?`, so the redis setnx/expire throttle logic is never exercised.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil and controller specs do not render views, so the test is green even though `best.html.erb` would raise on a nil `@topic_view`.
spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41 — The update test asserts on the in-memory `post.cooked` set by the before_save callback, so it passes even if the save silently failed and nothing was persisted.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — Third-party snippet hard-requires a pre-existing `#discourse-comments` element and has no null guard, so `comments.appendChild` throws and kills the whole embed if the div is missing or the script runs before it.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — Undocumented contract that the host page's `discourseUrl` global must end in a slash; without it the iframe src is silently built as `...comembed/best` and the embed 404s.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1 — New third-party-facing asset ships with no route, no precompile entry and no docs in this change, so embedding sites have no stable URL to include it from.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — postMessage sender check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` substring matching instead of an origin equality comparison, so any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl` satisfies the resize contract.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 — stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` introduces a new top-level stylesheet with no corresponding `config.assets.precompile` entry in this change, which raises on the framed page in production.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The `{type,height}` resize message carries no protocol version and is emitted only once on `window.onload`, so a parent page pinned to this contract keeps a stale iframe height after late/lazy content loads.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The new public `embed/best` boundary gates on exact `request.referer` host equality against a single `embeddable_host` setting, so www/apex variants or referrer-stripped requests get a hard InvalidAccess page rendered inside the customer's iframe.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is assigned only after both `raise` statements, so every error response on this deliberately-framed endpoint keeps the default SAMEORIGIN and renders as a blocked blank frame with no diagnosable message.

app/models/post.rb:133 — Post#cook` return contract drifted: it now ignores its `*args` and returns the persisted `raw` attribute whenever `cook_method` is `raw_html`, so callers passing text other than `self.raw` silently get a different value back.
app/models/post.rb:136 — raw_html posts now short-circuit before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, silently removing an externally-consumed plugin extension point for those posts.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1` is advanced unconditionally even though `PostRevisor#revise!` returns `true` regardless of whether `@post.save(validate: false)` succeeded, so a failed update is permanently masked and never retried on later imports.
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — The documented `--category`/`-c` option was removed from the `disqus import` CLI with no deprecation path, breaking existing invocations that pass it.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — disqus import` silently changed contract: it now performs a live HTTP fetch per thread via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, loses the Disqus `created_at`, and drops every thread (and its comments) whose link is not http(s) or whose fetch/create returns nil.
lib/post_creator.rb:216 — The new public `cook_method` opt is not added to PostCreator's "Acceptable options" doc block (lines 10-33) that serves as the class's documented contract.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content` is nil for RSS2.0/Atom items that only supply description/summary/content:encoded (simple-rss items are Hashes whose method_missing returns nil), so `.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, with `retry: false`, silently aborts the whole feed poll mid-loop

app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — post.present?` cannot distinguish success from failure: PostCreator swallows its own ActiveRecord::Rollback and returns an unsaved Post, so a failed creation either silently drops the item or hits `TopicEmbed.create!` with nil post_id/topic_id (NOT NULL violation)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1 is updated unconditionally even though `PostRevisor#revise!` returns false (or its `save(validate: false)` fails) without raising, so a failed update is permanently recorded as imported and never retried

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` is nil when the imported post was deleted/trashed (no FK, no cleanup), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw` and kills the hourly poll

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` is unrescued, so any 404/timeout/redirect error propagates out of import_remote and aborts the caller (PollFeed has retry:false and loses the remaining items; the disqus thor task dies mid-import)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — wrapping PostCreator in an outer `Topic.transaction` makes PostCreator's inner `Post.transaction` a joined no-op, so its `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is swallowed without rolling anything back and a partially created topic can be committed
lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is not atomic; a crash or redis error between the two leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key that throttles that embed URL forever

lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — check-then-act on TopicEmbed existence (plus running PollFeed inline concurrently with the scheduled hourly job) races two importers of the same URL into a unique-index violation on embed_url that aborts the job

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — switching the topic creation to TopicEmbed.import_remote drops the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` previously passed to PostCreator, so imported threads are stamped with the current date while their replies keep the original dates

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:12 — nothing removes TopicEmbed rows when the topic/post is deleted, so a stale row keeps returning a dead topic_id here while TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve bails on the existing row, leaving the embed permanently broken with no re-import path

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — stray `if` in `<%- end if %>` compiles the header if/else into a modifier-if whose condition is the next output statement; it only renders because that expression is truthy, and it emits the following whitespace before the button

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — no nil check on `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`, so a missing container (or script placed above it) throws a TypeError and silently breaks the embed

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` emits an unconditional DROP TABLE first, silently destroying an existing topic_embeds table and all its rows; no other Discourse migration uses force.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true` added to the top_topics create_table means any DB where this migration is (re)run drops the live top_topics table and its data instead of failing loudly.

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — This migration already exists in the base commit (already released), so production DBs will never re-run it and only fresh databases pick up the edit — a silent schema/behaviour divergence, and the change is unrelated to this PR's embedding feature.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a column with a non-null DEFAULT on PostgreSQL 9.x (pg 0.15.1, Rails 3.2.12/4.0.2) rewrites the whole `posts` table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads/writes on the largest table for the duration; no batched/backfill-then-set-not-null approach is used.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — t.string :embed_url` becomes varchar(255) under the Rails 3.2/4.0 PG adapter, so feed/embed URLs longer than 255 chars raise PG::StringDataRightTruncation and abort TopicEmbed.import (hourly PollFeed job); :text or an explicit larger limit is needed.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4 — topic_id and post_id are NOT NULL with no default and no index, so the belongs_to lookups (e.g. TopicEmbed.where(topic_id: ...)) and orphan cleanup do sequential scans.

db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:5 — topic_id/post_id are NOT NULL in the DB but TopicEmbed only validates presence of embed_url and content_sha1, so a missing association surfaces as a raw PG NOT NULL violation rather than a validation error.

db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:33 — An already-released migration is edited for whitespace only and now ends without a trailing newline; the change is inert on existing DBs and just churns an immutable file.

db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Three schema changes land with no accompanying db/schema.rb or db/structure.sql regeneration in the diff (no such file is tracked in this working tree, so this could not be fully verified).

app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — <%- end if %>` has a stray trailing `if` that turns the header block into a modifier-if on the next output statement (a hard syntax error under plain ERB, silently reordered output under Erubis).

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — TopicRetriever instantiates and synchronously runs the scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})`, bypassing Sidekiq/Jobs::Base and making one embed page view import the entire feed.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs blocking outbound HTTP (`open(url).read`) plus Readability parsing directly inside an ActiveRecord model.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open` is called without `require 'open-uri'` in this file (only app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb requires it), so import_remote breaks whenever PollFeed has not been autoloaded first.
app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1 — require_dependency 'email/sender'` is unused leftover scaffolding; nothing in this job touches Email::Sender.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:5 — require_dependency 'post_creator'` and `'post_revisor'` are unused here; those constants are used by TopicEmbed, which requires neither.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — feed_key` (and the `digest/sha1` require that exists only for it) is dead code, never called from anywhere in the repo.
db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — Unrelated drive-by edit to an already-shipped migration adds `force: true`, which will DROP an existing top_topics table on re-run.
db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true` on a brand-new table is unnecessary and silently drops the table if it already exists.
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — Drive-by removal of the `--category` option and its lookup is an unrelated behavior change bundled into an embed-URL PR.

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — Switching the disqus importer to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` silently converts an offline XML import into one that HTTP-fetches every thread link, and drops the previous `created_at` handling.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Layout reaches into request state and interpolates `request.referer` unescaped into inline JS as the postMessage target origin, duplicating the referer/host knowledge already in EmbedController and embed.js.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — import` mutates the caller's `contents` argument in place with `contents << ...`, a hidden side effect on a passed-in string.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — The number of best posts to show is hardcoded as `{best: 5}` instead of a site setting alongside the new `embedding` settings group.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:28 — The 60-second retrieval throttle window is a magic constant duplicated in a comment rather than a site setting.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — The retriever hand-rolls `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...)` twice, duplicating lookup logic that already lives on the model (`topic_id_for_embed`, `import`).
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:25 — User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` is duplicated verbatim in lib/topic_retriever.rb:49.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:62 — The `a[href]` and `img[src]` rewrite loops in `absolutize_urls` are copy-pasted, and both only handle paths beginning with `/`.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` is an HTML-rewriting utility with no persistence concern living as a public class method on an ActiveRecord model.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:1 — require_dependency 'nokogiri'` misuses require_dependency (meant for autoloadable app/lib constants) on a bundled gem.
config/locales/server.en.yml:37 — The `embed.permalink` locale key is added but never referenced anywhere.
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:11 — @topic_view.posts.present?` is evaluated twice and the logo/base_url branding link is duplicated at lines 8 and 26.
lib/post_creator.rb:216 — cook_method` gets a bespoke one-off assignment instead of being added to the pass-through attribute whitelist two lines above.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — ensure_embeddable` mixes authorization checks with mutating the response `X-Frame-Options` header, so its name misdescribes what it does.
app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:10 — The 30-second auto-reload interval is a magic constant embedded in an inline script in the view.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — The undocumented `discourseUrl` global must carry a trailing slash or the iframe URL is malformed; there is no validation, default, or docs for either required global.
spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 — require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` is an unused copy-paste require in this spec.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — The test named "is 404 without an embed_url" actually trips the blank-embeddable_host branch, duplicating the very next test and never exercising the missing-param path.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — Spec asserts on `TopicRetriever.new` while the controller now calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so it silently depends on jobs running inline in the test env.
db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb:33 — Unrelated drive-by whitespace change to a shipped migration that also strips the trailing newline at EOF.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read` pulls an entire remote page into memory with no size cap or read timeout before Readability parses it.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — The whole RSS/Atom feed is downloaded and parsed into memory with no size cap or read timeout.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Every feed item is imported inline with no limit or batching, so one hourly job runs unbounded PostCreator/PostRevisor plus Nokogiri work.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Each cache-missed embed URL synchronously re-runs a full feed download, parse and import of all items inside the RetrieveTopic job.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 — The `feed_key` conditional-GET cache key is computed but never used, so the full feed is refetched and reparsed on every poll.
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:16 — Per-post `post.user`/avatar and `post.url` (post.topic) lookups inside the render loop are N+1 queries unless TopicView eager-loads them.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every request for a not-yet-imported embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no dedup, flooding the queue under embed traffic.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — RetrieveTopic runs the entire hourly PollFeed synchronously inside a web-request-triggered job, bypassing PollFeed's own retry:false and re-polling the whole feed on every Sidekiq retry.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — The feed item loop has no per-item rescue, so one bad item (nil content, RecordNotUnique, PostCreator failure) aborts every remaining item and retry:false drops them until the next hour.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` sets no open/read timeout, so an unresponsive feed host can hang a Sidekiq worker on connect indefinitely.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` in import_remote sets no open/read timeout, so a slow or hung embed host can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Network and feed-parse errors are unrescued and unlogged; with retry:false a single transient failure silently loses the whole hour's import.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — OpenURI::HTTPError / SocketError / Errno from the remote fetch are unrescued, so any 404, 500 or DNS failure fails RetrieveTopic and burns all 25 default Sidekiq retries.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The 60s redis throttle key is written before the retrieval runs and never cleared on failure, so Sidekiq's first retry (~15-45s later) is throttled into a silent no-op.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic; a crash or redis error between them leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks retrieval of that embed_url for non-staff.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Anonymous unauthenticated requests enqueue a RetrieveTopic job per request with no enqueue-time URL validation or rate limit, letting crawlers flood the Sidekiq queue.

app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Staff bypass the throttle entirely, so a logged-in admin's embed iframe reloading every 30s triggers an unthrottled full feed poll plus remote fetch on every reload.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever with no attempt cap, backoff, or terminal error state, and each reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic job.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The embed hard-fails with InvalidAccess whenever the browser strips or omits the Referer header, with no fallback signal to the parent page.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — URI(url)` in absolutize_urls is unrescued and raises InvalidURIError on feed URLs containing spaces or unescaped characters that still pass the line-11 regex, aborting the whole poll batch.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The entire remote response is buffered into memory via `open(url).read` with no size cap, risking worker OOM on a very large response.
app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — Raising InvalidParameters for a missing embed_url makes Sidekiq retry a permanently unsatisfiable poison job 25 times before dead-lettering it.
lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 — A missing or misconfigured embed_by_username user makes the job return successfully with no log, leaving the client stuck in the endless reload loop.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 — Same silent no-op when embed_by_username resolves to no user: the hourly job reports success while importing nothing.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Every feed item is imported with no per-run cap, so run time and DB write volume are unbounded for a large feed.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 — The hourly recurrence has no overlap guard, so a slow poll (no timeouts, unbounded items) can run concurrently with the next tick and race on the unique embed_url index.
app/models/topic_embed.rb:27 — When PostCreator fails the item is skipped without creating a TopicEmbed and without any log, so the import failure is invisible.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — No null check on `#discourse-comments`; if the container is absent or the script runs before it, `appendChild` throws and the embed silently never loads.
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the 'loading' render too, so a shared cache can keep serving the loading page after the topic already exists.

app/models/post.rb:133 — Post#cook returns the raw string verbatim for cook_method raw_html, bypassing the PrettyText/sanitize pipeline so third-party HTML (feed items, scraped pages) is stored in `cooked` and rendered as live markup.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — RSS/Atom item content is CGI.unescapeHTML'd and imported with no sanitization at all, so anything in the feed (including <script>) becomes executable HTML on the forum origin.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The embed/feed URL is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute, so an embed_url containing a quote (accepted by URI and by the host check) breaks out and injects event-handler attributes into the stored raw HTML.
app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — The public embed page renders `raw post.cooked`, which for raw_html-cooked posts is unsanitized remote HTML served from the Discourse origin.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control for this public endpoint rests entirely on the Referer header, which any non-browser client can spoof, so the embeddable_host restriction is not an authorization boundary.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — Setting X-Frame-Options to the non-standard "ALLOWALL" removes the site's framing protection for a page on the forum origin without any frame-ancestors/CSP allowlist limiting who may frame it.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — An unauthenticated request (only a forged Referer needed) enqueues a job that makes the server fetch a remote URL and create a topic/post as embed_by_username; the throttle key is per-URL, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote fetches a user-influenced URL with open-uri before any scheme check, and the embeddable_host allowlist in TopicRetriever is not re-applied after open-uri follows redirects, enabling SSRF to internal hosts/ports.
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Kernel#open is called on the feed_polling_url site setting with no scheme validation, so a value beginning with "|" executes a shell command as the Sidekiq user.
app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage handler validates the sender with a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of an exact origin comparison.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The attacker-supplied Referer header is interpolated into an inline script and used as the postMessage targetOrigin, tying a cross-origin trust decision to an untrusted request header.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24 — poll_feed` is stubbed out in all four examples, so the entire feed-parsing body (user lookup, `require 'simple-rss'`, `i.id` URL fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, `TopicEmbed.import`) has zero coverage.

spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" passes vacuously because `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false and short-circuits first; the same holds for the examples at lines 12 and 24, so deleting any one guard would not fail any of them.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" actually passes because `embeddable_host` defaults to blank and `ensure_embeddable` raises first, so `params.require(:embed_url)` is never reached and stays untested.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — No example asserts which template is rendered, so the `render 'loading'` branch is unverified — the test still passes if the controller rendered `best` instead.

spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33 — Every example stubs `perform_retrieve`, so the specs only verify the boolean guard in `retrieve`; the dedupe check, PollFeed re-run and `fetch_http`/`import_remote` path never execute.

lib/topic_retriever.rb:21 — retrieved_recently?` is short-circuited in three examples and mocked in the other two, so the redis `setnx`/`expire` throttle and the `no_throttle` option are never executed by any test.
app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic is added with no spec file at all; the `embed_url` presence raise and the `no_throttle: user.staff?` staff bypass are untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — An unauthenticated GET with any crafted embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job that creates a brand-new public topic, so distinct query strings on the allowed host give an attacker unlimited unthrottled topic/post creation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmbedController#best`, which is reachable via unauthenticated GET (`get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'`) and does not require a logged-in user (it passes `current_user.try(:id)` which can be nil). When no existing embed is found, it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` then calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which will create a topic/post via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` if the URL host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The only guard is a 60-second Redis throttle keyed by the full `@embed_url` string (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) and `TopicEmbed` uniqueness is also on the full `embed_url`. Therefore, an attacker can bypass throttling and uniqueness by varying the query string/path while keeping the same allowed host, causing repeated new topic/post creation (and even if throttled, they can still enqueue unlimited jobs). The referer check can be satisfied by forging the Referer header to the allowed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — url` is interpolated into `<a href='#{url}'>` with no escaping, so an attacker-supplied embed_url containing a quote (URI parses `https://host/p?x='/onmouseover='...` fine) injects attributes into a post that is later rendered raw.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the passed-in `url` is directly interpolated into an HTML string: `#{url}` (via the `embed.imported_from` translation) with no escaping. The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent a URL containing a single quote (allowed by Ruby’s URI parser per RFC2396 mark characters) or other HTML-breaking characters. The resulting `contents` is saved as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `raw_html`, bypassing the usual cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, making attribute injection/XSS via a crafted `embed_url` verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — Feed HTML is CGI.unescapeHTML'd (actively un-escaping `<script>`) and imported with cook_method raw_html and no sanitizer, so a feed item body becomes stored XSS for every viewer.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is taken from the RSS (`i.content`), passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML` (which will turn `<script>` into `<script>`), and then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(...), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. The new `Post#cook` method explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Additionally, the embed view renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so any unescaped HTML/JS from the feed becomes stored and executed for viewers. No sanitizer is applied in this path, making stored XSS a real issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — No per-item rescue: one bad item (e.g. a feed with no content:encoded makes `i.content` nil and `nil.scrub` raise) aborts the whole loop and, with `retry: false`, silently drops every remaining item.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The only access control on this public endpoint is `request.referer`, an attacker-supplied header, so the embeddable-host gate passes for any direct curl request while appearing to enforce framing.
lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — The return value of `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` is discarded, so a failed save is indistinguishable from an applied revision.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/post_revisor.rb` the code calls `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` and does not check its boolean return value (nor does it use `save!`). If the save fails (e.g., due to validations when `skip_validations` is false, or DB constraints), execution continues to `@post.save_reply_relationships` and `revise!` will proceed as if the revision was applied, making a failed persistence indistinguishable from success unless callers explicitly inspect `@post.errors`. This is a verifiable correctness issue in the shown code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:21 — revise!` returns true unconditionally once `should_revise?` passes, reporting success to callers even when the underlying save failed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show `PostRevisor#revise!` returning `true` unconditionally. In the shown snippet, `revise!` only explicitly returns `false` when `should_revise?` fails; otherwise its return value depends on whatever the last executed call returns (`revise_post` / `update_category_description`), which is not shown in the diff. While `update_post` now calls `@post.save(validate: ...)` without checking the result, the finding specifically claims `revise!` reports success (returns true) even if the save failed—this is not directly verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — content_sha1` is advanced with `update_column` regardless of whether `revise!` actually applied the revision, so a failed update is permanently masked from the line 34 change check and never retried.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally executes `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (it explicitly does so when `should_revise?` is false), and the new `PostRevisor#update_post` uses `@post.save(...)` which can also fail/return false without raising. Because `TopicEmbed.import` does not check the result of `revise!` (or whether the post was actually updated) before updating `content_sha1`, it can record the new sha1 even if the post was not revised. That would cause future imports to skip the update (sha1s match), effectively masking a failed revision and preventing retry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:23 — post.present?` is true even when PostCreator rolled back (it returns the unsaved Post object), so `TopicEmbed.create!` runs with a nil `post_id` and raises a NOT NULL violation instead of skipping.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` can be nil once the post is deleted (no FK, no dependent cleanup), and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire feed run.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then (if the SHA changed) `PostRevisor.new(post)` without checking `post` for presence. The migration creates `topic_embeds.post_id` with `null: false` but adds no foreign key, and the model has no `dependent:` cleanup, so it’s possible for a `topic_embeds` row to remain after its `posts` row is deleted. In that case `embed.post` returns `nil`, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` / subsequent `@post.acting_user = ...` will raise, which would indeed abort the feed polling loop/job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s and each reload re-enters `best` and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job, so any URL that can never be imported becomes a permanent self-amplifying job loop per open browser tab.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`. The loading template (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) runs `document.location.reload()` every 30s unconditionally. Each reload re-hits `embed#best` with the same `embed_url` and, if the embed still doesn’t exist (e.g., import keeps failing or can never succeed), it will enqueue another `retrieve_topic` job again and re-render `loading`, repeating indefinitely per open tab. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s Redis throttle that reduces actual remote fetches, it does not prevent the controller from enqueuing a job every 30s, so the repeated job creation loop is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — A regular job synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed, bypassing PollFeed's `sidekiq_options retry: false` so a poison feed is re-downloaded and re-imported on every RetrieveTopic retry.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. This does bypass `Jobs::PollFeed`’s `sidekiq_options retry: false` because PollFeed is not being enqueued/run by Sidekiq at all—it's just a Ruby method call. Any exception from `PollFeed#execute`/`#poll_feed` (e.g., `open(...)`/`SimpleRSS.parse`) will bubble up and fail whatever job/request invoked `TopicRetriever` (notably `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` via `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`), so retries will be governed by the caller, not PollFeed’s retry setting, potentially causing repeated re-download attempts on retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` is a TOCTOU check against the unique index: a concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic both pass it and the loser raises RecordNotUnique, killing the whole run.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The code performs a non-atomic “check then create” flow. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve it does `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then can proceed to `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` and/or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Separately, Jobs::PollFeed iterates items and calls `TopicEmbed.import`, which itself does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, runs `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. Because `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index (db/migrate/..._create_topic_embeds.rb), two concurrent workers/jobs (e.g., a scheduled PollFeed and a RetrieveTopic-triggered fetch) can both observe “no row”, both attempt `create!`, and the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent) since there is no rescue/retry. That would indeed abort the job/run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that throttles that embed_url forever, and the key is claimed before any work so failed retrievals are throttled like successful ones.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. Those two operations are not atomic; if the process crashes (or errors) after `setnx` but before `expire`, the key will exist without a TTL and `setnx` will keep failing, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` forever for that `embed_url` (permanent throttling). Also, the throttle key is set before any retrieval work is performed, so even a failed/no-op retrieval path (e.g., missing user in `fetch_http`) will still be throttled for 60 seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The throttle key embeds the full attacker-controlled embed_url, so unbounded distinct URLs of unbounded length produce unbounded distinct redis keys.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb `retrieved_recently?` constructs the Redis key as `retrieved:#{@embed_url}`. `@embed_url` comes from the request param `embed_url` (EmbedController#best) and, after only a host check (`URI(@embed_url).host` == `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), can still contain attacker-controlled, arbitrarily long path/query components and can be made unique per request. This will create distinct Redis keys per distinct URL and the key length is proportional to the URL length. Although the keys are set to expire after 60 seconds, an attacker can still cause a large number of unique keys (and/or very large keys) to be created within that window, leading to unbounded keyspace growth over time windows and potential memory/DoS impact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — no_throttle` is granted for any request carrying a staff session, so a logged-in staff member browsing an embedded page bypasses the 60s throttle and triggers a full synchronous feed poll on every page load.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` follows redirects without re-validating the host and ignores port/userinfo, so an open redirect on the embeddable host turns the public endpoint into an SSRF whose response body is imported into a public post.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) on an attacker-influenced `url` (via `TopicRetriever.fetch_http` from the public `/embed/best?embed_url=...` flow). `TopicRetriever.invalid_host?` only validates the *initial* URL’s `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but `open-uri` will automatically follow HTTP redirects and the redirected-to host is not re-validated anywhere. That means if a URL on the allowed embeddable host redirects to an internal host/IP, Discourse will fetch that content server-side and import it into a post (`TopicEmbed.import(...)`), creating a verifiable SSRF risk. (The “ignores port/userinfo” part is partially true: host-only validation ignores port, but userinfo spoofing like `allowed.com@internal` would not pass because `URI.host` would be `internal`.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — revise!` is called without `bypass_bump`, so a source page whose HTML changes on every fetch bumps the topic to the top of the latest list every hour forever.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import’s update path (app/models/topic_embed.rb), when the fetched content changes it calls `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, ..., skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` but does not pass any option to prevent bumping (e.g. `bypass_bump`). Since PollFeed is scheduled hourly and `content_sha1` is recomputed from the fetched HTML, a source that changes slightly on each fetch will repeatedly trigger `revise!`. In Discourse, `PostRevisor` supports a bypass bump option specifically to avoid topic bumps on automated edits; omitting it here means these automated revisions can keep bumping the topic in “latest” indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — cook` returns raw verbatim for raw_html posts with no allowlist, and the flag is sticky, so every later edit of that post by any user is also stored unsanitized.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook` + plugin filters). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true`, and `TopicEmbed.import` updates use `PostRevisor.revise!` without changing `cook_method`, so the raw_html flag persists across later edits. As a result, the post’s `cooked` content can remain verbatim `raw` HTML on every subsequent cook, with no allowlist/sanitization step in this path, which is a verifiable XSS/security risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_creator.rb:216 — :cook_method` is now forwarded from arbitrary PostCreator opts, so any caller that passes user-controlled params through can request the sanitizer-bypassing raw_html mode.

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — The `revise!` + `update_column` pair runs outside any transaction, so a crash between them leaves the post revised while the sha1 stays stale and the item is re-revised on the next poll.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is updated (`content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`), it calls `revisor.revise!` (which persists changes to the associated post) and then separately calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. There is no surrounding transaction in this update path, so if the process crashes or errors after the post revision is saved but before `update_column` runs, `topic_embeds.content_sha1` remains stale. On the next poll, the code will again see a mismatch and re-run the revision. This atomicity gap is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — params.require(:embed_url)` accepts non-strings, so `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` turns the lookup into an IN-clause matching an unrelated topic and `embed_url[k]=v` produces an unhandled 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` only enforces presence, not type. Rails will happily provide an Array for `embed_url[]=a&embed_url[]=b` or a Hash for `embed_url[k]=v`. That value is passed directly to `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, which does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url)`: with an Array this becomes an `IN (...)` query (so it can return a topic for a different URL than intended), and with a Hash it can raise an exception during SQL/quoting, resulting in an unhandled 500. There is no type check/coercion in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:35 — Every test mocks `poll_feed`, so the feed fetch, parsing, per-item error handling and import path have zero coverage and stay green regardless of production behaviour.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb all examples are for `execute` and use `poller.expects(:poll_feed)` (never/once), so none of the new `poll_feed` implementation in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb (open-uri fetch, SimpleRSS.parse, iterating items, calling TopicEmbed.import) is exercised by these specs. The statement about per-item error handling is a bit overstated (there isn’t any explicit error handling code to cover), but the core claim that the feed fetch/parse/import path has zero test coverage due to mocking is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:34 — Both throttle tests stub `retrieved_recently?`, so the redis setnx/expire throttle logic is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the two examples under "with a valid host" explicitly stub `topic_retriever.expects(:retrieved_recently?).returns(false/true)` and then assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. Because `retrieved_recently?` is stubbed, the Redis-based throttle implementation inside `retrieved_recently?` (the `$redis.setnx` / `expire` logic added in lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never executed by these tests, so that behavior is untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:50 — TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil and controller specs do not render views, so the test is green even though `best.html.erb` would raise on a nil `@topic_view`.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the example "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" sets `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` but does not specify a return value. With Mocha, an expected call without `.returns(...)` will return `nil`, so the controller assigns `@topic_view = nil`. Rails controller specs typically don’t render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so the spec can pass even though `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` calls `@topic_view.posts` and would raise `NoMethodError` if rendered in this test setup. This is a real defect in the test (it should return a mock/double TopicView), even though production would normally get a real `TopicView` instance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:41 — The update test asserts on the in-memory `post.cooked` set by the before_save callback, so it passes even if the save silently failed and nothing was persisted.

app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — Third-party snippet hard-requires a pre-existing `#discourse-comments` element and has no null guard, so `comments.appendChild` throws and kills the whole embed if the div is missing or the script runs before it.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code immediately executes, does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')`, and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. There is no null/undefined guard, so if the element is missing (or the script runs before that element is in the DOM), `comments` will be null and `appendChild` will throw, breaking the embed script.

In `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), when an existing embed’s content changes it does:

- `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(...), skip_validations: true, ...)`
- then **unconditionally** `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`.

From the diff to `PostRevisor`, `update_post` now calls `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. With `skip_validations: true`, this becomes `@post.save(validate: false)`, and the return value is not checked anywhere (neither in `update_post` nor in `revise!`). `save` can return `false` without raising (e.g., callbacks aborting the save), yet `TopicEmbed` will still persist the new `content_sha1`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post` is nil when the imported post was deleted/trashed (no FK, no cleanup), so `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises NoMethodError on `@post.raw` and kills the hourly poll

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` is unrescued, so any 404/timeout/redirect error propagates out of import_remote and aborts the caller (PollFeed has retry:false and loses the remaining items; the disqus thor task dies mid-import)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — wrapping PostCreator in an outer `Topic.transaction` makes PostCreator's inner `Post.transaction` a joined no-op, so its `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is swallowed without rolling anything back and a partially created topic can be committed

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` wrapping `PostCreator.new(...).create` inside `Topic.transaction`, but it does not show (or guarantee) that `PostCreator` opens an inner `Post.transaction` or that it raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback` in a way that would be “swallowed” and allow a partial commit. In Rails, a nested (joinable) `transaction` is not a no-op with respect to rollback semantics: raising `ActiveRecord::Rollback` inside the block marks the whole transaction for rollback; it does not typically result in a partial commit. The proposed failure mode depends on implementation details of `PostCreator` not present in this diff and also mischaracterizes typical nested-transaction behavior, so it’s not a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx followed by a separate expire is not atomic; a crash or redis error between the two leaves a TTL-less `retrieved:<url>` key that throttles that embed URL forever

adjudication.rationale:
In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle is implemented as:

```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
  return false
end
```

Because `SETNX` and `EXPIRE` are separate Redis commands, a process crash or Redis/network error after `setnx` but before `expire` can leave `retrieved:<url>` permanently set with no TTL. Since subsequent calls will see the key exists and return `true` (throttled), that embed URL could be throttled indefinitely. This is a real correctness/availability problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:37 — check-then-act on TopicEmbed existence (plus running PollFeed inline concurrently with the scheduled hourly job) races two importers of the same URL into a unique-index violation on embed_url that aborts the job

In `TopicEmbed.import`, creation is also check-then-act (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` then `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction). With concurrent importers (e.g., the scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` running at the same time as an on-demand `TopicRetriever`, or multiple retrievers for different URLs where PollFeed imports the same one), two processes can both observe no existing row and both attempt `create!`, causing the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` to raise (e.g., `RecordNotUnique`) and abort the job/request since there’s no rescue/retry logic shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — switching the topic creation to TopicEmbed.import_remote drops the `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` previously passed to PostCreator, so imported threads are stamped with the current date while their replies keep the original dates

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — Adding a column with a non-null DEFAULT on PostgreSQL 9.x (pg 0.15.1, Rails 3.2.12/4.0.2) rewrites the whole `posts` table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads/writes on the largest table for the duration; no batched/backfill-then-set-not-null approach is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — Layout reaches into request state and interpolates `request.referer` unescaped into inline JS as the postMessage target origin, duplicating the referer/host knowledge already in EmbedController and embed.js.
matched_golden_ids: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

This is the same core problem as the golden comment, since `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme+host+port) and using the full referrer URL is incorrect and can cause messages to be dropped (e.g., breaking resizing).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Every feed item is imported inline with no limit or batching, so one hourly job runs unbounded PostCreator/PostRevisor plus Nokogiri work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Each cache-missed embed URL synchronously re-runs a full feed download, parse and import of all items inside the RetrieveTopic job.

Since `RetrieveTopic` enqueues `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`, every cache-miss/new embed URL handled by that job can trigger a full feed download/parse/import pass, which is a clear performance/correctness concern introduced by this diff (feed polling is no longer only hourly/scheduled; it can run per embed retrieval).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Every request for a not-yet-imported embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job with no dedup, flooding the queue under embed traffic.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading`.
