adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — RetrieveTopic runs the entire hourly PollFeed synchronously inside a web-request-triggered job, bypassing PollFeed's own retry:false and re-polling the whole feed on every Sidekiq retry.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `perform_retrieve` directly calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, instead of enqueuing it as a scheduled Sidekiq job. That means PollFeed’s `sidekiq_options retry: false` is not in effect here (it only applies when Sidekiq runs the job), and the full feed poll (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` + iterating all `rss.items`) can be executed as part of the web-request-triggered `retrieve_topic` flow (EmbedController enqueues `:retrieve_topic`, which calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`). If the enclosing `RetrieveTopic` job retries (it has no `retry: false`), each retry would re-run this synchronous feed polling as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — The feed item loop has no per-item rescue, so one bad item (nil content, RecordNotUnique, PostCreator failure) aborts every remaining item and retry:false drops them until the next hour.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, rss.items.each processes items without any per-item exception handling. Inside the loop it does `i.content.scrub` and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`; if `i.content` is nil (possible for some RSS/Atom items) this will raise, and any exception from `TopicEmbed.import` (e.g., `create!` hitting the unique index on `embed_url` in a race, or other runtime errors) will abort the entire job, preventing remaining items from being processed in that run. The job is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a failure won’t be retried by Sidekiq and the skipped items won’t be attempted again until the next scheduled hourly run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` sets no open/read timeout, so an unresponsive feed host can hang a Sidekiq worker on connect indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using open-uri with no timeout options (e.g., `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`). This is a real reliability risk introduced by the diff: if the feed endpoint is slow/unresponsive, the Sidekiq worker executing PollFeed can be tied up waiting on the network call for an extended period (depending on Ruby/Net::HTTP defaults and OS behavior), reducing throughput.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url)` in import_remote sets no open/read timeout, so a slow or hung embed host can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote calls `open(url).read` without passing explicit `open_timeout`/`read_timeout` options, but the finding’s claim that it can “block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely” is not verifiable from the diff alone. Ruby’s `open-uri` uses `Net::HTTP`, which has default timeouts (commonly 60s for open/read) unless explicitly changed, so this is at most a potential for slower-than-desired jobs, not an indefinite hang proven by the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Network and feed-parse errors are unrescued and unlogged; with retry:false a single transient failure silently loses the whole hour's import.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` without any `rescue`. Both `open-uri` (network/HTTP errors, timeouts) and `SimpleRSS.parse` (malformed feed) can raise, which will abort the job. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a transient failure will not be retried and the import for that scheduled run is lost until the next recurrence. The “unlogged” part is overstated because Sidekiq/Rails typically log exceptions, but the lack of handling combined with `retry: false` is a real robustness issue introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — OpenURI::HTTPError / SocketError / Errno from the remote fetch are unrescued, so any 404, 500 or DNS failure fails RetrieveTopic and burns all 25 default Sidekiq retries.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote` the code does `open(url).read` (open-uri) and then parses with `Readability::Document.new(...)` without any rescue. Network/HTTP failures like `OpenURI::HTTPError`, `SocketError`, `Errno::*`, timeouts, etc. will raise and bubble up to callers. `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (new in the diff) calls `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which can call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `fetch_http`, and `RetrieveTopic` does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so these exceptions will fail the Sidekiq job and trigger Sidekiq’s default retry behavior (commonly 25 retries). Thus a persistent 404/DNS failure will repeatedly retry and eventually exhaust retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26 — The 60s redis throttle key is written before the retrieval runs and never cleared on failure, so Sidekiq's first retry (~15-45s later) is throttled into a silent no-op.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, `retrieve` calls `perform_retrieve` only if `retrieved_recently?` returns false. `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis key (`setnx` + `expire 60`) *before* any network work happens, and there is no ensure/rescue to clear it on exceptions. Since `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (added in the diff) will be Sidekiq-retried by default on failure, a first attempt that raises during `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` (e.g., `open` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) will be retried within ~15–45s but then `retrieved_recently?` will return true and `retrieve` will become a no-op and also not raise, effectively swallowing the retry and delaying retrieval until the 60s TTL expires. This behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic; a crash or redis error between them leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks retrieval of that embed_url for non-staff.

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only afterward given a TTL via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two commands are not atomic. If the process crashes or a Redis/network error occurs after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` is executed, the key will remain without a TTL, and future calls will see `setnx` fail and treat it as "retrieved recently" forever (unless manually deleted), permanently blocking retrieval for non-staff. This defect is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — Anonymous unauthenticated requests enqueue a RetrieveTopic job per request with no enqueue-time URL validation or rate limit, letting crawlers flood the Sidekiq queue.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil it unconditionally calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url) and renders loading. There is no authentication requirement in the controller, and the only guard is ensure_embeddable, which relies on request.referer matching SiteSetting.embeddable_host (a client-controlled header) and does not validate embed_url beyond presence. The RetrieveTopic job itself only checks embed_url.present?; host/URI validation and throttling happen later inside TopicRetriever#retrieve, meaning every request can still enqueue a Sidekiq job even if it will immediately no-op. This makes it feasible for crawlers/attackers (or even traffic from the embeddable host) to flood the queue with RetrieveTopic jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:17 — Staff bypass the throttle entirely, so a logged-in admin's embed iframe reloading every 30s triggers an unthrottled full feed poll plus remote fetch on every reload.

app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8 — The loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s forever with no attempt cap, backoff, or terminal error state, and each reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic job.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, the controller unconditionally enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `embed/loading`. The loading view (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`) contains a `setTimeout` that calls `document.location.reload()` every 30s with no cap/backoff/terminal state. Therefore, if the embed is not created (e.g., remote fetch fails, settings misconfigured, or takes a long time), the browser will keep reloading and each request will enqueue another `RetrieveTopic` job. While `TopicRetriever` has a 60s throttle on doing work, it does not prevent repeated job enqueues from repeated reloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — The embed hard-fails with InvalidAccess whenever the browser strips or omits the Referer header, with no fallback signal to the parent page.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. When the `Referer` header is missing/stripped, `request.referer` is `nil`, `URI('')` yields a `nil` host, and the comparison fails, triggering the exception. This is directly exercised by the added spec (`"raises an error with no referer"`). With this exception path, it won’t render the embed layout/script that posts a resize message to the parent, so there is no fallback communication to the parent page in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — URI(url)` in absolutize_urls is unrescued and raises InvalidURIError on feed URLs containing spaces or unescaped characters that still pass the line-11 regex, aborting the whole poll batch.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import` only validates `url` with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which will accept strings like `"http://example.com/a b"` (contains spaces/unescaped chars) that still start with `http://`. It then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, where `uri = URI(url)` is executed without any rescue. `URI(...)` can raise `URI::InvalidURIError` for such URLs, and this exception would propagate up through `TopicEmbed.import` into `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (or other callers), aborting processing of the feed loop/job.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — The entire remote response is buffered into memory via `open(url).read` with no size cap, risking worker OOM on a very large response.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb `import_remote` does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`, which reads the entire HTTP response body into a Ruby string with no explicit limit or streaming. This is verifiable from the diff and can cause excessive memory use / potential OOM in the worker if the remote URL serves a very large document.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:10 — Raising InvalidParameters for a missing embed_url makes Sidekiq retry a permanently unsatisfiable poison job 25 times before dead-lettering it.

adjudication.rationale: The new job does raise `Discourse::InvalidParameters` when `args[:embed_url]` is missing, and it does not set `sidekiq_options retry: false`. However, within this diff the only enqueue site (`EmbedController#best`) requires `embed_url` via `params.require(:embed_url)` and passes it through (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`), so the “missing embed_url” situation does not arise from the added/changed code paths. The claim about Sidekiq retrying a poison job 25 times is also dependent on Sidekiq/global job configuration not shown in the diff. As written, the finding is a hypothetical operational concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:50 — A missing or misconfigured embed_by_username user makes the job return successfully with no log, leaving the client stuck in the endless reload loop.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it does `user = User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then `return if user.blank?`. If `embed_by_username` is unset/empty or points to a non-existent user, the retrieval path silently no-ops (no exception, no log, no embed created). In `EmbedController#best`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`, whose view reloads the page every 30s. Since the embed is never created, each reload repeats this forever, producing an endless reload loop with no feedback. This behavior is directly verifiable from the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26 — Same silent no-op when embed_by_username resolves to no user: the hourly job reports success while importing nothing.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `user = User.where(...).first` and then `return if user.blank?`, with no log/exception. So the job will indeed “succeed” while importing nothing if the configured `embed_by_username` doesn’t resolve. However, this is not clearly a defect introduced by the diff: if no such user exists, there is nothing valid to post as, and silently skipping may be an intentional, acceptable behavior for a scheduled job rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — Every feed item is imported with no per-run cap, so run time and DB write volume are unbounded for a large feed.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no limit, pagination, or cutoff (e.g., by published date/last-modified). For a feed that returns a very large number of items, each hourly run will iterate all items and perform at least a lookup per item (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`) and potentially create/update posts, making runtime and DB activity scale with feed size and effectively unbounded per run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:11 — The hourly recurrence has no overlap guard, so a slow poll (no timeouts, unbounded items) can run concurrently with the next tick and race on the unique embed_url index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Jobs::PollFeed` is scheduled hourly and performs a potentially slow/unbounded `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items` without an explicit timeout or lock in this job. However, the finding’s core claim—"no overlap guard" leading to concurrent executions that race on the unique `topic_embeds.embed_url` index—depends on the behavior of `Jobs::Scheduled` / the scheduler framework, which is not shown in the diff. From the diff alone, we can’t verify that scheduled jobs can overlap or that there isn’t already a built-in overlap/locking mechanism. Therefore the concurrency/unique-index race aspect is not a strictly verifiable defect from this change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:27 — When PostCreator fails the item is skipped without creating a TopicEmbed and without any log, so the import failure is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import the code does `post = creator.create` and only creates a TopicEmbed if `post.present?`, with no explicit logging in the `else` case. However, whether this produces a silent/invisible failure depends on PostCreator#create’s behavior (outside this diff): if it raises on failure, the error would not be “invisible” (it would bubble/log via exception handling); if it returns nil without raising, then it would be silent. Because the finding’s core claim hinges on behavior not shown in the diff, it is not a strictly verifiable defect from the patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:12 — No null check on `#discourse-comments`; if the container is absent or the script runs before it, `appendChild` throws and the embed silently never loads.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the code does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then unconditionally calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);`. If the element with id `discourse-comments` is missing (or the script executes before it exists in the DOM), `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime error, preventing the embed from loading. There is no guard or deferred execution beyond the immediate IIFE.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied to the 'loading' render too, so a shared cache can keep serving the loading page after the topic already exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called unconditionally after the `if/else` that either builds `@topic_view` or `render 'loading'`. That means the loading response is also marked cacheable for 1 minute. Since the loading page is served from the same URL (`/embed/best?embed_url=...`), an intermediary/shared cache could continue serving the cached loading HTML even after `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` starts returning a topic id, causing users (and the page’s 30s reload loop) to keep seeing the loading page until the cache entry expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — Post#cook returns the raw string verbatim for cook_method raw_html, bypassing the PrettyText/sanitize pipeline so third-party HTML (feed items, scraped pages) is stored in `cooked` and rendered as live markup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb). New import paths set this mode: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw` coming directly from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.content` after `CGI.unescapeHTML`) or scraped HTML (`TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `ruby-readability` on `open(url).read`). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). This combination bypasses the existing PrettyText/sanitization pipeline and outputs third-party HTML as live markup, which is a verifiable XSS/security risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — RSS/Atom item content is CGI.unescapeHTML'd and imported with no sanitization at all, so anything in the feed (including <script>) becomes executable HTML on the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the feed item body is taken from `i.content`, run through `CGI.unescapeHTML(...)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. As a result, arbitrary HTML from the RSS/Atom feed (including `<script>` or event-handler attributes) can be stored and later rendered as executable HTML on the Discourse origin (e.g., embed view uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — The embed/feed URL is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted href attribute, so an embed_url containing a quote (accepted by URI and by the host check) breaks out and injects event-handler attributes into the stored raw HTML.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an HTML snippet containing the provided `url` directly into a single-quoted `href`: `"#{url}"`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows URLs containing a literal apostrophe `'` in the path/query (RFC3986 sub-delims; Ruby `URI` can parse such URLs, and the host check in `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`). A crafted URL like `http://eviltrout.com/'onmouseover='alert(1)` would pass the regex and host check, and when interpolated would break out of the `href` attribute and inject a new attribute (e.g., `onmouseover`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, this becomes stored/served HTML injection (XSS) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — The public embed page renders `raw post.cooked`, which for raw_html-cooked posts is unsanitized remote HTML served from the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a `cook_method` mode `:raw_html` where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from remote RSS/readability content with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), but `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `href`/`src` and does not sanitize HTML. The embed view then renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and for these posts `post.cooked == post.raw`, so remote HTML is injected into the response unescaped. That is a verifiable XSS risk served from the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — Access control for this public endpoint rests entirely on the Referer header, which any non-browser client can spoof, so the embeddable_host restriction is not an authorization boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is allowed/denied solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and otherwise raising). The `Referer` header is client-controlled and can be spoofed by non-browser clients or altered by intermediaries, so this check is not a reliable authorization boundary for the public `GET /embed/best` endpoint. No other server-side auth/secret is used to enforce the “only this host can embed” restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — Setting X-Frame-Options to the non-standard "ALLOWALL" removes the site's framing protection for a page on the forum origin without any frame-ancestors/CSP allowlist limiting who may frame it.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — An unauthenticated request (only a forged Referer needed) enqueues a job that makes the server fetch a remote URL and create a topic/post as embed_by_username; the throttle key is per-URL, so varying the query string bypasses it entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, there is no authentication check; it only gates access via ensure_embeddable which compares the Referer host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host (a forgeable header). If TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) returns nil, it enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic with the provided embed_url even when current_user is nil. The job calls TopicRetriever#retrieve, which throttles using a Redis key that includes the full URL string ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}"), so changing the query string produces a different key and bypasses the 60s throttle. Because TopicRetriever only checks host equality with SiteSetting.embeddable_host, an attacker can still trigger repeated remote fetches and creation of new topics/posts (TopicEmbed.import_remote/import) for many distinct embed_url variants on that host, posted as SiteSetting.embed_by_username.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — import_remote fetches a user-influenced URL with open-uri before any scheme check, and the embeddable_host allowlist in TopicRetriever is not re-applied after open-uri follows redirects, enabling SSRF to internal hosts/ports.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed.import_remote, which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) directly on the passed-in `url` with no scheme validation in that method. The main caller path is user-influenced: `EmbedController#best` takes `params.require(:embed_url)` and enqueues retrieval; `TopicRetriever` only checks `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` before calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. However, `open-uri` will follow HTTP redirects, and after redirect there is no re-validation that the final destination host/port is still within the allowlist. Thus an allowed host that redirects (or is controlled) could cause server-side fetching of internal/other hosts (SSRF). This is a concrete, verifiable issue in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — Kernel#open is called on the feed_polling_url site setting with no scheme validation, so a value beginning with "|" executes a shell command as the Sidekiq user.

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the job does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` after requiring `open-uri`, but it only checks the setting is present (and enabled) and does not validate that the value is an http/https URL. In Ruby, `Kernel#open` treats strings starting with `|` as a command to execute via a pipe, so a `feed_polling_url` value like `"|rm -rf /"` would execute a shell command in the Sidekiq process context. This is a verifiable command-injection risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — The postMessage handler validates the sender with a substring test (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)) instead of an exact origin comparison.

app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — The attacker-supplied Referer header is interpolated into an inline script and used as the postMessage targetOrigin, tying a cross-origin trust decision to an untrusted request header.

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:24 — poll_feed` is stubbed out in all four examples, so the entire feed-parsing body (user lookup, `require 'simple-rss'`, `i.id` URL fallback, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, `TopicEmbed.import`) has zero coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests that `execute` gates calling `poll_feed` based on settings; it does not exercise the `poll_feed` implementation (RSS parsing, URL fallback, unescape/scrub, `TopicEmbed.import`). However, that is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect in the production code introduced by the diff. Also, `poll_feed` is not “stubbed out” in all four examples; they set expectations on whether it’s invoked, not a stub of its body.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18 — "requires feed_polling_url" passes vacuously because `feed_polling_enabled?` defaults to false and short-circuits first; the same holds for the examples at lines 12 and 24, so deleting any one guard would not fail any of them.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" actually passes because `embeddable_host` defaults to blank and `ensure_embeddable` raises first, so `params.require(:embed_url)` is never reached and stays untested.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController` has `before_filter :ensure_embeddable`, and `ensure_embeddable` raises immediately when `SiteSetting.embeddable_host.blank?`. In `config/site_settings.yml` the new `embeddable_host` default is `''` (blank). The spec `it "is 404 without an embed_url" do; get :best; ...` does not stub `embeddable_host` or a valid referer, so the request fails in the before_filter before `best` runs and before `params.require(:embed_url)` can raise. The example therefore doesn’t actually test the missing-`embed_url` behavior it describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40 — No example asserts which template is rendered, so the `render 'loading'` branch is unverified — the test still passes if the controller rendered `best` instead.

spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33 — Every example stubs `perform_retrieve`, so the specs only verify the boolean guard in `retrieve`; the dedupe check, PollFeed re-run and `fetch_http`/`import_remote` path never execute.

adjudication.rationale: The spec at spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb only exercises the guard logic in `TopicRetriever#retrieve` by asserting whether `perform_retrieve` is called and by stubbing `retrieved_recently?`. It does not execute `perform_retrieve`, so paths inside it (dedupe `TopicEmbed.where(...).exists?`, optional `Jobs::PollFeed` invocation, and `fetch_http`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote`) are indeed untested by this spec. However, this is a test coverage/design critique rather than a functional bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff; the diff doesn’t show broken behavior, only limited test scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:21 — retrieved_recently?` is short-circuited in three examples and mocked in the other two, so the redis `setnx`/`expire` throttle and the `no_throttle` option are never executed by any test.

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the first three examples never reach retrieved_recently? because invalid_host? returns true (embeddable_host nil/different or invalid URL), and in the “with a valid host” context both examples stub retrieved_recently? to return true/false. Therefore the real implementation of retrieved_recently? (including the $redis.setnx/expire throttle and the early return for @opts[:no_throttle]) is never exercised by any test added in this diff. This is a verifiable test coverage gap introduced/left by the diff (not a runtime bug per se).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:9 — Jobs::RetrieveTopic is added with no spec file at all; the `embed_url` presence raise and the `no_throttle: user.staff?` staff bypass are untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` but does not add a corresponding spec file for that job, so it’s true that this specific job behavior isn’t directly unit-tested in the diff. However, “missing a spec”/“untested branches” is a test coverage/process concern, not a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the code itself that can be verified as failing or incorrect from the diff alone. The diff also adds broader coverage around embed retrieval via `TopicRetriever` and `EmbedController` specs, so the absence of a dedicated `RetrieveTopic` spec is not inherently a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:39 — "Supports updating the post" asserts only `cooked =~ /new contents/`, which still passes if `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, ...)`, `absolutize_urls`, `skip_validations` or `bypass_rate_limiter` were dropped from the revise path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a spec `it "Supports updating the post"` that only asserts `post.cooked` contains `new contents`. While it’s true this single assertion would not catch future regressions where the revise path stops updating `content_sha1`, stops absolutizing URLs, or changes options like `skip_validations`/`bypass_rate_limiter`, that is a test-strength/coverage critique rather than a verifiable defect in the code introduced by this diff. Nothing in the diff indicates those behaviors were dropped or are currently broken; the test simply doesn’t assert them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:34 — No example re-imports identical content, so the `content_sha1 !=` short-circuit (skip revision for unchanged feed items) is entirely uncovered and could be deleted without failing a test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds logic in `TopicEmbed.import` to skip revising an existing embedded post when `content_sha1` hasn’t changed (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). The new spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only covers: (1) malformed URL returns nil, (2) first-time import, and (3) updating when content changes. There is no test that re-imports the *same* URL with *identical* `contents` and asserts that no revision occurs / `content_sha1` short-circuits. Therefore that branch/behavior is currently untested and could be removed without any existing test failing, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:56 — absolutize_urls` is only exercised with leading-slash `href`/`src`; the non-default-port prefix branch, protocol-relative `//host/x` (which this code rewrites to `<prefix>/host/x`), and relative URLs without a leading slash are uncovered.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is rewritten by stripping all leading slashes (`sub(/^\/+/, '')`) and then prefixing with `"#{prefix}/"`. For a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/x`, this produces `"#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/x"` (e.g., `https://site.com/cdn.example.com/x`), which is incorrect. This behavior is directly implied by the code in the diff, and the provided spec only covers single-leading-slash paths (e.g., `/hello`), not `//...`, non-default ports, or other relative URL forms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:78 — topic_id_for_embed` is mocked out in the controller spec and never exercised against real rows, so a broken lookup (wrong column, missing `.first`) would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: The controller spec does stub `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`, so it doesn’t exercise the DB lookup from that spec. In the diff, `topic_id_for_embed` is implemented as `where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`, which is a correct and working lookup against real rows. adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — @post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])` changes revision behaviour for every caller but no PostRevisor spec was added or changed, and the topic_embed update example uses content that passes validation anyway.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` from always running validations (`@post.save`) to conditionally skipping them when `opts[:skip_validations]` is true (`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`). That is a real behavior change, but it appears intentional and is directly used by new code in the diff (`TopicEmbed.import` calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`). The proposed finding’s main complaint (no spec added/changed for PostRevisor, and the existing TopicEmbed spec not covering failing validations) is about test coverage and expectations, not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff demonstrates this causes incorrectness or a security issue on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:35 — Shared `response.should be_success` / X-Frame-Options assertions live in an `after` block, which runs before mocha verification and is silently discarded when the example body has already failed.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the shared `response.should be_success` and `X-Frame-Options` assertions are placed in an `after` hook inside the "success" context. In RSpec, `after(:each)` hooks still run even when the example body fails, and failures in `after` are reported (not silently discarded). Also, while mocha expectation verification typically runs at the end of an example, its ordering relative to user-defined `after` hooks is an implementation detail and does not make the assertions incorrect or ineffective in a verifiable way from this diff. This is more of a test-structure preference than a real defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41 — TopicEmbed.expects(:topic_id_for_embed)` and `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` carry no `.with(...)`, so a wrong `embed_url` or `user_id` passed through `Jobs.enqueue` would not be caught.

adjudication.rationale: While it’s true the spec uses `expects(...)` without `.with(...)`, the proposed finding is not a verifiable defect in the diff. In `EmbedController#best`, the code does **not** call `TopicRetriever.new` at all; it enqueues a job: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. Therefore the spec’s expectations around `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` are themselves inconsistent with the controller implementation, and the complaint about missing `.with(...)` arguments does not identify a concrete bug introduced by the diff (it’s at most a test strictness suggestion, and also based on an apparent misread of what the controller does).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:29 — The `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` branch (malformed referer) is uncovered; only the blank-host and nil-referer paths are tested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ensure_embeddable` with a `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` path, and the new controller spec exercises missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, and `nil` referer (which goes through `URI('')` and does not raise `URI::InvalidURIError`). There is indeed no test that supplies a malformed referer that would trigger `URI::InvalidURIError`. However, this is a test coverage observation, not a bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; the rescue branch existing without a direct spec is not itself a verifiable runtime problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — The new raw_html `cook` branch is only covered indirectly on create; the update example's `/new contents/` regex would still pass if the branch were removed, so the revise path is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new `Post#cook` early return for `cook_method == :raw_html`, and the specs in `topic_embed_spec` do assert on create that `post.cooked == post.raw`, which directly exercises that branch for the initial cook. The proposed finding is about the *strength* of the update test (it might still pass if the branch were removed), i.e., test coverage quality, not a verifiable runtime bug/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The revise path in `TopicEmbed.import` does not change `cook_method`, so it would remain `:raw_html` from creation; nothing in the diff demonstrably breaks revise behavior.
